title.zh: 卷七十七 酷吏列傳
title.raw: 卷七十七 酷吏列傳 Volume 77: Biographies of Cruel Officials

sentences.zh: 汉承战国余烈，多豪猾之民。

translations.literal: The Han inherited the lingering fierceness of the Warring States era, and its people included many bold and crafty sorts.
translations.idiomatic: The Han took over a world still marked by the Warring States, and among its people were many who were bold, ruthless, and cunning.

sentences.zh: 其并兼者则陵横邦邑，桀健者则雄张闾里。

translations.literal: Those who annexed others then overawed and trampled the towns and districts; those who were fierce and strong lorded it over their neighborhoods.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful swallowed weaker neighbors and rode roughshod over whole districts; the violent and the able made themselves masters of every lane and ward.

sentences.zh: 且宰守旷远，户口殷大。

translations.literal: Moreover, the magistrates who governed were stationed far away, while registered households were exceedingly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the officials set over the people held sway across vast distances, and the population within their registers was immense.

sentences.zh: 故临民之职，专事威断，族灭奸轨，先行后闻。

translations.literal: Therefore those charged with overseeing the people devoted themselves to awe-inspiring decisions, exterminating whole clans for treacherous wrongdoing, acting first and reporting afterward.
translations.idiomatic: So those who held authority over common folk leaned on terror and arbitrary judgment: they wiped out entire families for alleged villainy, struck first, and asked permission only later.

sentences.zh: 肆情刚烈，成其不桡之威。

translations.literal: They gave rein to harsh, unbending temperaments and thereby forged an awe that would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: They indulged their own harshness and forged a reputation for inflexible terror.

sentences.zh: 违众用己，表其难测之智。

translations.literal: They defied the multitude and followed their own judgment, displaying a cleverness none could fathom.
translations.idiomatic: They brushed aside consensus, trusted only themselves, and cultivated an air of inscrutable cunning.

sentences.zh: 至于重文横入，为穷怒之所迁及者，亦何可胜言。

translations.literal: When, moreover, legal formulas were twisted to ensnare people, and men became the objects of rage pushed to its limit—how can such cases even be fully told?
translations.idiomatic: When the law was stretched to trap the innocent and men were swept up by fury run past all bounds, the toll became literally beyond words.

sentences.zh: 故乃积骸满{穴井}，漂血十里。

translations.literal: Thus bones piled until they filled the pits, and blood floated for ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses were heaped until the burial pits overflowed, and blood ran in streams for miles.

sentences.zh: 致温舒有虎冠之吏，延年受屠伯之名，岂虚也哉！

translations.literal: Hence Wang Wenshu gained clerks likened to tiger-capped officers, and Yan Nian earned the name “butcher-broker”—could that have been empty rumor?
translations.idiomatic: So it was that Wang Wenshu produced underlings called “tiger-hatted” enforcers, and Yan Nian won the nickname “the butcher’s broker”—and those reputations were no idle tales.

sentences.zh: 若其揣挫强伤，摧勒公卿，碎裂头脑而不顾，亦为壮也。

translations.literal: As for those who humbled the mighty and wounded the strong, who broke and drove the high ministers and shattered skulls without a second thought—that too could be called heroic.
translations.idiomatic: There were also men who humbled the powerful, humiliated grandees, and split skulls without flinching—acts the age could only call bold.

sentences.zh: 自中兴以后，科网稍密，吏人之严害者，方于前世省矣。

translations.literal: From the restoration onward, the net of statutes grew somewhat tighter, and cruel clerks, compared with earlier generations, were somewhat fewer.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, the legal net drew a little tighter, and clerks notorious for savagery were somewhat less common than in former times.

sentences.zh: 而阉人亲娅，侵虐天下。

translations.literal: Yet eunuchs and their kinsmen by marriage oppressed and ravaged the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet eunuchs and their in-laws ran rampant and tyrannized the empire.

sentences.zh: 至使阳球磔王甫之尸，张俭剖曹节之墓。

translations.literal: It reached the point that Yang Qiu dismembered the corpse of Wang Fu, and Zhang Jian opened the tomb of Cao Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Matters went so far that Yang Qiu had Wang Fu’s corpse torn apart, and Zhang Jian broke open the tomb of Cao Jie.

sentences.zh: 若此之类，虽厌快众愤，亦云酷矣！

translations.literal: Cases of this sort, though they slaked the crowd’s thirst for vengeance, were cruel indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Such deeds may have gratified popular rage, but they were cruelty all the same.

sentences.zh: 俭知名，故附《党人篇》。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian was a man of renown, and so he is appended in the “Partisans” chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang Jian was already a celebrated figure, his story is attached to the chapter on the partisan prohibition.

sentences.zh: 董宣字少平，陈留圉人也。

translations.literal: Dong Xuan, courtesy name Shaoping, was a native of Yu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xuan, whose courtesy name was Shaoping, came from Yu in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 初为司徒侯霸所辟，举高第，累迁北海相。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned by Minister of Education Hou Ba, ranked at the top of his class, and rose in stages to Prefect of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: He was first recommended by Minister of Education Hou Ba, placed first in the high-ranking group, and eventually promoted step by step to Prefect of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 到官，以大姓公孙丹为五官掾。

translations.literal: When he took office, he appointed the great clan head Gongsun Dan as his aide for the five offices.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving he named the powerful local magnate Gongsun Dan as his aide for the five offices.

sentences.zh: 丹新造居宅，而卜工以为当有死者，丹乃令其子杀道行人，置尸舍内，以塞其咎。

translations.literal: Dan had newly built a residence, and the diviner said someone must die there; Dan then ordered his son to kill a passerby on the road, place the corpse inside the house, and thereby ward off the ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Dan had just finished a new house when the geomancer declared that a death was fated to occur there; Dan then told his son to murder a traveler, leave the body in the building, and so “answer” the omen.

sentences.zh: 宣知，即收丹父子杀之。

translations.literal: When Xuan learned of it, he at once arrested Dan and his sons and put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Xuan found out, he immediately seized Gongsun Dan and his sons and executed them.

sentences.zh: 丹宗族亲党三十余人，操兵诣府，称冤叫号。

translations.literal: More than thirty kinsmen and partisans of Dan’s clan took up arms, went to the prefectural headquarters, and cried out that they had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Over thirty members of Gongsun Dan’s lineage and their allies armed themselves, marched to the yamen, and loudly protested their innocence.

sentences.zh: 宣以丹前附王莽、虑交通海贼，乃悉收系剧狱，使门下书佐水丘岑尽杀之。

translations.literal: Xuan, because Dan had formerly adhered to Wang Mang and he feared collusion with coastal bandits, then arrested them all and held them in the jail for serious criminals, ordering his clerk Shuiqiu Cen to kill every one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xuan, recalling that Gongsun Dan had once served Wang Mang and fearing he might be in league with pirates, jailed the lot in the prison for capital cases and ordered his clerk Shuiqiu Cen to slaughter them all.

sentences.zh: 青州以其多滥，奏宣考岑，宣坐征诣廷尉。

translations.literal: Qing Province, deeming the killings excessive, memorialized to have Xuan and Cen interrogated under torture; Xuan was therefore summoned to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial authorities of Qingzhou, judging the bloodshed excessive, reported Dong Xuan and had him and Shuiqiu Cen tortured for confession; Dong Xuan was consequently cited to the capital commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 在狱，晨夜讽诵，无忧色。

translations.literal: In prison he recited texts morning and night and showed no sign of worry.
translations.idiomatic: In his cell he chanted the classics day and night and never lost his composure.

sentences.zh: 及当出刑，官属具馔送之，宣乃厉色曰：“董宣生平未曾食人之食，况死乎！

translations.literal: When the time came for him to go out to execution, his subordinates prepared a farewell meal; Xuan then said sternly, “In all my life Dong Xuan has never eaten another man’s food—how much less at the hour of death!
translations.idiomatic: When his execution drew near, his staff set out a parting feast; Dong Xuan said sharply, “Dong Xuan has never eaten at another’s expense in his life—least of all on the way to his death!

sentences.zh: ”升车而去。

translations.literal: ” He mounted the cart and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he climbed into the cart and rode away.

sentences.zh: 时，同刑九人，次应及宣，光武驰使驺骑特原宣刑，且令还狱。

translations.literal: At that time nine men were to suffer the same sentence, and when his turn should have reached Xuan, Guangwu sent mounted couriers at full gallop especially to spare Xuan from execution and ordered him returned to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Nine others were condemned with him, and when the roll call would next have fallen on Dong Xuan, Emperor Guangwu sent relay riders at a gallop to commute his sentence and had him sent back to jail.

sentences.zh: 遣使者诘宣多杀无辜，宣具以状对，言水丘岑受臣旨意，罪不由之，愿杀臣活岑。

translations.literal: He dispatched an envoy to rebuke Xuan for having killed many innocents; Xuan set forth the facts in reply, saying that Shuiqiu Cen had acted on his orders, that the fault was not Cen’s, and that he wished to die in Cen’s place and let Cen live.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial messenger was sent to upbraid him for slaughtering the guiltless; Dong Xuan laid out the whole affair, declared that Shuiqiu Cen had merely obeyed his commands, that the blame lay with himself, not with Cen, and begged to die so that Cen might live.

sentences.zh: 使者以闻，有诏左转宣怀令，令青州勿案岑罪。

translations.literal: When the envoy reported this, an edict came demoting Xuan to Magistrate of Huai and ordering Qingzhou not to prosecute Cen.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger relayed his words; an edict followed, demoting Dong Xuan to magistrate of Huai county and forbidding Qingzhou to pursue charges against Shuiqiu Cen.

sentences.zh: 岑官至司隶校尉。

translations.literal: Cen rose in office to Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Shuiqiu Cen eventually rose to become colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 后江夏有剧贼夏喜等寇乱郡境，以宣为江夏太守。

translations.literal: Later, when serious bandits such as Xia Xi ravaged the territory of Jiangxia, Xuan was appointed Prefect of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when outlaws like Xia Xi threw Jiangxia into chaos, the court named Dong Xuan prefect of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 到界，移书曰：“朝廷以太守能禽奸贼，故辱斯任。

translations.literal: When he reached the border he sent a document saying, “The court believes the prefect capable of seizing villainous bandits, and for that reason has burdened me with this office.
translations.idiomatic: At the frontier he issued a circular: “The court thinks its prefect can catch traitorous bandits, which is why I have been given this post.

sentences.zh: 今勒兵界首，檄到，幸思自安之宜。

translations.literal: Now I have drawn up troops at the border; when this summons reaches you, I hope you will weigh what course would secure your own safety.”
translations.idiomatic: I have now massed troops on the border; when you read this order, consider carefully how you may keep yourselves safe.”

sentences.zh: ”喜等闻，惧，即归降散。

translations.literal: When Xi and the others heard, they were afraid and at once submitted and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Xi and his fellows heard this, panic overtook them; they surrendered at once and scattered.

sentences.zh: 外戚阴氏为郡都尉，宣轻慢之，坐免。

translations.literal: A member of the imperial in-law Yin clan held the post of Commandant of the commandery; Xuan slighted him and was removed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman of the Yin consort clan served as commandant; Dong Xuan treated him with contempt and lost his post as a result.

sentences.zh: 后特征为洛阳令。

translations.literal: Later he was specially summoned to serve as Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later specially called to office as magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 时湖阳公主苍头白日杀人，因匿主家，吏不能得。

translations.literal: At that time a slave of the Princess of Huyang had killed a man in broad daylight and then hidden in the princess’s household, so the clerks could not seize him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a household slave of the Princess of Huyang had murdered someone in daylight and then taken refuge in her mansion, beyond the clerks’ reach.

sentences.zh: 及主出行，而以奴骖乘，宣于夏门亭候之，乃驻车叩马，以刀画地，大言数主之失，叱奴下车，因格杀之。

translations.literal: When the princess went out, she had the slave ride as her outrider; Xuan waited for her at the Summer Gate pavilion, stopped the carriage, seized the horse’s bridle, scored the ground with his knife while loudly enumerating the princess’s faults, ordered the slave to get down, and then struck him dead.
translations.idiomatic: When she rode out with the killer as her side attendant, Dong Xuan ambushed her at the Summer Gate watchpost, halted her team, seized the bridle, traced lines on the earth with his blade while shouting her misdeeds aloud, forced the slave from the cart, and beat him to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 主即还宫诉帝，帝大怒，召宣，欲箠杀之。

translations.literal: The princess at once returned to the palace to complain to the emperor, who was furious and summoned Xuan, intending to beat him to death with clubs.
translations.idiomatic: She hurried to the palace to denounce him; the emperor flew into a rage, summoned Dong Xuan, and meant to club him to death.

sentences.zh: 宣叩头曰：“愿乞一言而死。

translations.literal: Xuan kowtowed and said, “I beg leave to speak one sentence before I die.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xuan kowtowed and said, “Grant me one word before I die.”

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“欲何言？

translations.literal: The emperor said, “What would you say?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, “What is it?”

sentences.zh: ”宣曰：“陛下圣德中兴，而从奴杀良人，将何以理天下乎？

translations.literal: Xuan said, “Your Majesty’s sacred virtue restored the dynasty; if you let a slave kill an innocent commoner, how will you order the realm?”
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xuan replied, “Your Majesty’s sagely power brought the house back from ruin; if a slave may slaughter the guiltless, how are you to govern all under Heaven?”

sentences.zh: 臣不须箠，请得自杀。

translations.literal: “I have no need of clubs; allow me to take my own life.”
translations.idiomatic: “I need no beating from you; let me kill myself.”

sentences.zh: ”即以头击楹，流血被面。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon struck his head against a pillar until blood covered his face.
translations.idiomatic: He then dashed his head against a column until his face ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 帝令小黄门持之，使宣叩头谢主，宣不从，强使顿之，宣两手据地，终不肯俯。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a minor eunuch to restrain him and told Xuan to kowtow and apologize to the princess; Xuan refused, and when they forced him to bow his head, he braced both hands on the ground and would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told a young eunuch to hold him back and ordered Dong Xuan to bow in apology to the princess; he would not. They tried to press his head down, but he planted both hands on the floor and never lowered his brow.

sentences.zh: 主曰：“文叔为白衣时，臧主匿死，吏不敢至门。

translations.literal: The princess said, “When Wenshu was a commoner, he hid condemned men for me, and clerks dared not come to my gate.
translations.idiomatic: The princess cried, “When Wenshu was still a commoner, he concealed fugitives for me, and no bailiff dared knock at my door.

sentences.zh: 今为天子，威不能行一令乎？

translations.literal: Now that he is Son of Heaven, can his authority not reach even one magistrate?”
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is Son of Heaven, can his power not reach a single county magistrate?”

sentences.zh: ”帝笑曰：“天子不与白衣同。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, “The Son of Heaven is not the same as a commoner.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, “The Son of Heaven is not a commoner.”

sentences.zh: ”困敕强项令出。

translations.literal: ” He then ordered the “stiff-necked magistrate” dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He then told the “stubborn-necked magistrate” to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 赐钱三十万，宣悉以班诸吏。

translations.literal: He granted three hundred thousand cash, which Xuan distributed entirely among his clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He awarded three hundred thousand cash; Dong Xuan handed every coin to his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 由是搏击豪强，莫不震栗。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he struck at the mighty, none failed to tremble.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever he moved against the powerful, they quaked with fear.

sentences.zh: 京师号为“卧虎”。

translations.literal: The capital nicknamed him the “Crouching Tiger.”
translations.idiomatic: The capital dubbed him the “crouching tiger.”

sentences.zh: 歌之曰：“枹鼓不鸣董少平。

translations.literal: They sang of him, “The drum is never sounded for Dong Shaoping.”
translations.idiomatic: A ditty ran: “You never hear the drum while Dong Shaoping is in charge.”

translations.literal: The line closes the quotation mark that ends the popular verse.
translations.idiomatic: Here the people’s rhyme about Dong Shaoping breaks off.

sentences.zh: 在县五年。

translations.literal: He remained in the county for five years.
translations.idiomatic: He served five years in that county.

sentences.zh: 年七十四，卒于官。

translations.literal: At age seventy-four he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 诏遣使者临视，唯见布被覆尸，妻子对哭，有大麦数斛、敝车一乘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered an envoy to attend his funeral; they found only a cloth quilt covering the corpse, his wife and children weeping opposite him, several hu of barley, and one broken-down cart.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent an inspector to his home; all they saw was a hemp sheet over the body, his wife and children weeping beside it, a few measures of barley, and a single rickety cart.

sentences.zh: 帝伤之，曰：“董宣廉洁，死乃知之！

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and said, “Dong Xuan was incorrupt; only after his death did I know it!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken and said, “Dong Xuan was honest—I learned it only when he was gone!

sentences.zh: ”以宣尝为二千石，赐艾绶，葬以大夫礼。

translations.literal: ” Because Xuan had once held a two-thousand-dan post, he was granted the ai ribbon and buried with the rites due a grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Because Dong Xuan had once borne rank at two thousand piculs, he was given the mottled ribbon and buried with ceremonies fit for a high minister.

sentences.zh: 拜子并为郎中，后官至齐相。

translations.literal: His son Bing was appointed gentleman of the palace and later rose to Prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dong Bing was made a gentleman of the palace and eventually became prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 樊晔字仲华，南阳新野人也。

translations.literal: Fan Ye, courtesy name Zhonghua, was a native of Xinye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye, courtesy name Zhonghua, hailed from Xinye in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 与光武少游旧。

translations.literal: In youth he roamed about with Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In his younger days he had been Guangwu’s companion on the road.

sentences.zh: 建武初，征为侍御史，迁河东都尉，引见云台。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was summoned as attendant censor, promoted to commandant of Hedong, and granted audience in the Cloud Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu reign he was called up as attendant censor, advanced to commandant of Hedong, and received an audience in the Cloud Terrace.

sentences.zh: 初，光武微时，尝以事拘于新野，晔为市吏，餽饵一笥，帝德之不忘，仍赐晔御食，及乘舆服物。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guangwu was still obscure, he had once been detained at Xinye for an affair; Ye, then a market clerk, sent him a basket of cakes, and the emperor remembered the kindness and never forgot it, later bestowing on Ye imperial viands and garments from the imperial wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when Guangwu was still unknown, he had been held at Xinye over some matter; Fan Ye, then a market inspector, sent a hamper of food, and the emperor cherished the deed ever after, later presenting him with dishes from the palace kitchen and clothing from the imperial wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 因戏之曰：“一笥饵得都尉，何如？

translations.literal: He then teased him, saying, “A basket of cakes for a commandant—how does that bargain strike you?”
translations.idiomatic: He joked, “One hamper of snacks bought you a commandant’s commission—fair trade?”

sentences.zh: ”晔顿首辞谢。

translations.literal: Ye kowtowed and declined with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye kowtowed and demurred.

sentences.zh: 及至郡，诛讨大姓马適匡等。

translations.literal: When he reached the commandery, he executed and extirpated the great clan heads Ma Shi Kuang and the like.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he wiped out powerful houses such as that of Ma Shi Kuang.

sentences.zh: 盗贼清，吏人畏之。

translations.literal: Banditry was cleared away, and clerks and commoners feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Robbery ceased, and both officials and townsfolk stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 数年，迁杨州牧，教民耕田种树理家之术。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Governor of Yang Province, where he taught the people methods of plowing fields, planting trees, and managing their households.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he became governor of Yang province and instructed the populace in farming, arboriculture, and household economy.

sentences.zh: 视事十余年，坐法左转积长。

translations.literal: After more than ten years in office he broke the law and was demoted to chief of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He governed for over a decade, then ran afoul of the statutes and was reduced to chief of Ji canton.

sentences.zh: 隗嚣灭后，陇右不安，乃拜晔为天水太守。

translations.literal: After Wei Ao was destroyed, the Longyou region remained unsettled, and Ye was appointed Prefect of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Ao had been crushed and the Longyou frontier was still restless, Fan Ye was named prefect of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 政严猛，好申、韩法、善恶立断。

translations.literal: His government was harsh and severe; he favored the methods of Shen Buhai and Han Fei and settled good and evil in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was fierce; he loved the legalism of Shen Buhai and Han Fei and judged guilt or innocence on the spot.

sentences.zh: 人有犯其禁者，率不生出狱，吏人及羌胡畏之。

translations.literal: Anyone who violated his prohibitions generally did not leave prison alive; clerks, commoners, Qiang, and Hu all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who broke his bans rarely emerged from jail alive; officials, townsfolk, Qiang, and Hu alike dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 道不拾遗。

translations.literal: Nothing picked up on the road was kept.
translations.idiomatic: Lost goods were left untouched in the street.

sentences.zh: 行旅至夜，聚衣装道傍，曰“以付樊公”。

translations.literal: Travelers who came by night would pile their baggage by the roadside, saying, “Leave it for Lord Fan.”
translations.idiomatic: Wayfarers arriving after dark heaped their packs beside the road, saying, “This is for Lord Fan to guard.”

sentences.zh: 凉州为之歌曰：“游子常苦贫，力子天所富。

translations.literal: Liang Province sang of him, “The wanderer always knows bitter poverty; the diligent son is Heaven’s favorite.
translations.idiomatic: A song in Liang province ran: “The roamer knows bitter want; the toiling man is Heaven’s rich.”

sentences.zh: 宁见乳虎穴，不入冀府寺。

translations.literal: Better see a suckling tiger in its den than enter the yamen of the Ji prefect.”
translations.idiomatic: “Better face a tigress in her lair than walk into Fan’s headquarters in Ji.”

sentences.zh: 大笑期必死，忿怒或见置。

translations.literal: Great laughter means you are sure to die; rage may yet let you go.”
translations.idiomatic: “If he laughs loud, you are dead for certain; if he glares in fury, you might still be spared.”

sentences.zh: 嗟我樊府君，安可再遭值！

translations.literal: Alas for our Lord Fan of the prefecture—how could we meet with you again!”
translations.idiomatic: “Alas, our prefect Lord Fan—would that we never crossed your path again!”

sentences.zh: ”视事十四年，卒官。

translations.literal: ” He held office fourteen years and died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He served fourteen years and died in office.

sentences.zh: 永平中，显宗追思晔在天水时政能，以为后人莫之及，诏赐家钱百万。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era, Emperor Ming, recalling Fan Ye’s administrative ability in Tianshui, thought no later man had matched him and edicted a gift of a million cash to his family.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping, Emperor Ming looked back on Fan Ye’s record at Tianshui, decided no successor had equaled him, and ordered a million cash sent to his household.

sentences.zh: 子融，有俊才，好黄、老，不肯为吏。

translations.literal: His son Rong had outstanding talent, loved Huang-Lao learning, and would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan Rong was brilliantly gifted, devoted to Huang-Lao thought, and refused a career in government.

sentences.zh: 李章字第公，河内怀人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhang, courtesy name Digong, was a native of Huai in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang, courtesy name Digong, came from Huai in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 五世二千石。

translations.literal: For five generations his family had held two-thousand-dan posts.
translations.idiomatic: For five generations his forebears had borne rank at two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 章习《严氏春秋》，经明教授，历州郡吏。

translations.literal: Zhang studied the Gongyang commentary in Yan’s tradition, mastered the classics, taught students, and served successively as a clerk in provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang studied the Yan school’s Gongyang commentary, excelled in the canon, instructed disciples, and worked his way through posts in various provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 光武为大司马，平定河北，召章置江曹属，数从征伐。

translations.literal: When Guangwu was grand marshal and was pacifying Hebei, he summoned Zhang and placed him on the staff of the river office, and Zhang repeatedly accompanied the campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: While Guangwu served as grand marshal and was bringing Hebei to heel, he called Li Zhang to his staff in charge of river works, and Zhang rode with him on many expeditions.

sentences.zh: 光武即位，拜阳平令。

translations.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, Zhang was appointed Magistrate of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangwu mounted the throne, Li Zhang became magistrate of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 时赵、魏豪右往往屯聚，清河大姓赵纲遂于县界起坞壁，缮甲兵，为在所害。

translations.literal: At that time the powerful families of Zhao and Wei often gathered in armed bands, and the great Zhao surname of Qinghe, Zhao Gang, then raised fortifications on the county border, repaired armor and weapons, and became a scourge to the region.
translations.idiomatic: In those days magnates of Zhao and Wei commonly mustered private forces, and Zhao Gang, a powerful clan of Qinghe, threw up a fortified stockade on the county line, outfitted troops, and terrorized the countryside.

sentences.zh: 章到，乃设飨会，而延谒纲。

translations.literal: When Zhang arrived, he set a banquet and courteously invited Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang’s first move was to host a feast and politely summon Zhao Gang.

sentences.zh: 纲带文剑，被羽衣，从士百余人来到。

translations.literal: Gang wore an inscribed sword, draped a feathered cloak, and arrived with more than a hundred followers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gang came with a patterned sword, a feathered robe, and over a hundred armed retainers.

sentences.zh: 章与对宴饮，有顷，手剑斩纲，伏兵亦悉杀其从者，因驰诣坞壁，掩击破之，吏人遂安。

translations.literal: Zhang feasted and drank with him; after a while he drew his sword and beheaded Gang, while concealed soldiers slew all his attendants; he then galloped to the stockade, stormed and broke it, and thereafter clerks and people were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang drank with him awhile, then suddenly drew his blade and struck off Zhao Gang’s head while hidden troops cut down every follower; he raced to the fort, stormed it flat, and peace returned to the district.

sentences.zh: 迁千乘太守，坐诛斩盗贼过滥，征下狱免。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Prefect of Qiansheng but, because he had executed bandits beyond proper measure, was summoned, imprisoned, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to prefect of Qiansheng, then cited for excessive slaughter in suppressing bandits, jailed, and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 岁中拜侍御史，出为琅邪太守。

translations.literal: Within the year he was appointed attendant censor and sent out as Prefect of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: The same year he became attendant censor and was posted as prefect of Langye.

sentences.zh: 时北海安丘大姓夏长思等反，遂囚太守处兴，而据营陵城。

translations.literal: At that time the great families of Anqiu in Beihai, Xia Changsi and others, rebelled, imprisoned Prefect Chu Xing, and seized the city of Yingling.
translations.idiomatic: Then the magnates of Anqiu in Beihai—Xia Changsi and his confederates—rose in revolt, jailed Prefect Chu Xing, and occupied Yingling.

sentences.zh: 章闻，即发兵千人，驰往击之。

translations.literal: When Zhang heard the news, he at once raised a thousand troops and galloped to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang heard the news, immediately mobilized a thousand men, and rode to strike them.

sentences.zh: 掾史止章曰：“二千石行不得出界，兵不得擅发。

translations.literal: His clerks remonstrated, “A two-thousand-dan official may not leave his jurisdiction, nor may troops be raised without authorization.”
translations.idiomatic: His aides warned him, “A prefect may not cross his border, and you have no orders to call out soldiers.”

sentences.zh: ”章按剑怒曰：“逆虏无状，囚劫郡守，此何可忍！

translations.literal: Zhang gripped his sword in wrath and said, “These traitors have seized our prefect—how can I endure it!
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhang clutched his sword and roared, “Rebels have kidnapped the governor—how can I stand by?

sentences.zh: 若坐讨贼而死，吾不恨也。

translations.literal: If I die punishing rebels, I will have no regret.”
translations.idiomatic: If I die putting down outlaws, I will not regret it.”

sentences.zh: ”遂引兵安丘城下，募勇敢烧城门，与长思战，斩之，获三百余级，得牛马五百余头而还。

translations.literal: ” He therefore led his troops beneath the walls of Anqiu, recruited the bold to burn the gates, fought Changsi, beheaded him, took more than three hundred heads, and captured five hundred-odd head of cattle and horses before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He led his force to Anqiu, enlisted daredevils to torch the gates, fought Xia Changsi, cut off his head, claimed over three hundred enemy heads, and drove home five hundred-odd cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 兴归郡，以状上帝，悉以所得班劳吏士。

translations.literal: When Xing returned to the commandery, he reported the affair to the emperor, who ordered all the booty distributed to reward clerks and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Xing was back in his yamen, he memorialized the whole affair; the emperor had every prize shared out to reward the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 后坐度人田不实征，以章有功，但司冠论。

translations.literal: Later he was convicted for having surveyed others’ fields untruthfully in connection with tax levies; because Li Zhang had merit, he was only remanded to the Minister of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: He was later found guilty of misreporting land surveys used for taxation, but on account of Li Zhang’s past service the court merely handed him over to the Minister of Justice for judgment instead of harsher punishment.

sentences.zh: 月余免刑，归。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was spared corporal punishment and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he was released from torture and sent home.

sentences.zh: 复征，会病卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned again, but fell ill and died before reporting.
translations.idiomatic: The court called him back to office, yet he sickened and died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 周䊸字文通，下邳徐人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Xu, courtesy name Wentong, was a native of Xu in Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xu, whose courtesy name was Wentong, came from Xu county in Xiapi; the histories write his surname with the rare graph 䊸.

sentences.zh: 为人刻削少恩，好韩非之术。

translations.literal: In person he was harsh and grudging of kindness, and he loved the techniques of Han Fei.
translations.idiomatic: He was cutting and seldom merciful, and he delighted in Han Fei’s brand of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 少为廷尉史。

translations.literal: In his youth he served as a clerk in the office of the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a clerk under the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 永平中，补南行唐长。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he was appointed chief of Nanxingtang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping reign he was posted as chief of Nanxingtang canton.

sentences.zh: 到官，晓吏人曰：“朝廷不以长不肖，使牧黎民，而性仇猾吏，志除豪贼，且勿相试！

translations.literal: When he took office he declared to the clerks and people: “The court did not appoint this chief because he lacks talent, to shepherd the black-haired masses, yet my nature hates crafty clerks and my purpose is to extirpate powerful bandits—do not put me to the test!”
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he told his staff and the populace: “The throne did not give me this magistracy for my mediocrity, to care for the common folk; I loathe slippery underlings and mean to destroy powerful criminals—so do not try my patience!”

sentences.zh: ”遂杀县中尤无状者数十人，吏人大震。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon executed several dozen of the most outrageous men in the county, and clerks and commoners were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: With that he put several dozen of the county’s worst offenders to death, and everyone in the yamen quaked.

sentences.zh: 过博平令。

translations.literal: He passed through service as Magistrate of Boping.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as magistrate of Boping.

sentences.zh: 收考奸臧，无出狱者。

translations.literal: He arrested and examined corrupt wrongdoers, and none left the prison alive.
translations.idiomatic: He jailed and tortured corrupt criminals until not one emerged from custody alive.

sentences.zh: 以威名迁齐相，亦颇严酷，专任刑法，而善为辞案条教，为州内所则。

translations.literal: Because of his awe-inspiring name he was promoted to Chancellor of Qi; he too was quite harsh and cruel, relying solely on penal statutes, yet he excelled at drafting legal instruments and instructions and became the model for the province.
translations.idiomatic: His fearsome reputation won him promotion to chancellor of Qi; he was likewise severe, leaning entirely on the criminal code, yet he was a master of written charges and regulations that the whole province imitated.

sentences.zh: 后坐杀无辜，复左转博平令。

translations.literal: Later, for killing innocents, he was again demoted to Magistrate of Boping.
translations.idiomatic: He was later stripped of rank for slaughtering the guiltless and sent back down to magistrate of Boping.

sentences.zh: 建初中，为勃海太守。

translations.literal: In the Jianchu era he became Prefect of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianchu he was named prefect of Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 每敕令到郡，辄隐闭不出，先遣使属县尽决刑罪，乃出诏书。

translations.literal: Whenever an edict reached the commandery, he would hide it and not issue it, first dispatching agents through the subordinate counties to finish executing all capital sentences, only then producing the imperial document.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an imperial order arrived, he would seal it away, send runners through every county to clear the jails of condemned men, and only then let the edict be read aloud.

sentences.zh: 坐征诣廷尉，免归。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Commandant of Justice, dismissed, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was cited to the capital commandant of justice, removed from office, and returned to private life.

sentences.zh: 䊸廉洁无资，常筑□以自给，肃宗闻而怜之，复以为郎，再迁召陵侯相。

translations.literal: Xu was incorrupt but lacked resources, often building □ to support himself; Emperor Zhang heard of it and pitied him, appointed him gentleman again, and twice promoted him to Chancellor of the Marquis of Zhaoling district.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xu was honest but poor, and he often molded sun-dried bricks to feed himself, the damaged text of the chapter leaving the exact word unreadable; Emperor Zhang took pity, restored him as a gentleman of the court, and twice advanced him to chancellor of the Zhaoling marquis’s estate.

sentences.zh: 廷掾惮䊸严明，欲损其威，乃晨取死人断手足，立寺门。

translations.literal: The commandery aide feared Xu’s severity and wished to undermine his authority; at dawn they took a dead man, severed his hands and feet, and set him upright at the gate of the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery aide, terrified of Xu’s strictness, tried to humiliate him by planting a mutilated corpse at the courthouse gate before daybreak.

sentences.zh: 䊸闻，便往至死人边。

translations.literal: When Xu heard of it, he went straight to the side of the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the stunt, Xu walked directly to the body.

sentences.zh: 若与死人共语状。

translations.literal: He acted as if he were holding conversation with the dead.
translations.idiomatic: He behaved as though he were speaking with the dead man.

sentences.zh: 阴察视口眼有稻芒，乃密问守门人曰：“悉谁载藁入城者？

translations.literal: Secretly examining the mouth and eyes, he found husks of grain; he then quietly asked the gatekeeper, “Who in all has brought sheaves of straw into the city?”
translations.idiomatic: Peering closely, he noticed rice awns in the corpse’s mouth and eyes; he whispered to the gatekeeper, “Exactly who has been hauling hay through this gate?”

sentences.zh: ”门者对：“唯有廷掾耳。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper answered, “Only the commandery aide.”
translations.idiomatic: The gateman said, “Only the commandery aide.”

sentences.zh: ”又问铃下：“外颇有疑令与死人语者不？

translations.literal: He again asked his runners, “Outside, are there many who suspect the magistrate of talking with the dead?”
translations.idiomatic: He asked his escort, “Do many people out there think I am chatting with a corpse?”

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“廷掾疑君。

translations.literal: They replied, “The commandery aide suspects you.”
translations.idiomatic: They answered, “The commandery aide thinks so.”

sentences.zh: ”乃收廷掾考问，具服“不杀人，取道边死人。

translations.literal: ” He then arrested the commandery aide and examined him under torture; the man confessed in full: “I did not kill anyone; I took a corpse from beside the road.”
translations.idiomatic: He seized the aide and pressed him until he admitted, “I killed no one—I dragged in a body from the roadside.”

sentences.zh: ”后人莫敢欺者。

translations.literal: ” Afterward none dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on no one tried to fool him again.

sentences.zh: 征拜洛阳令。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court called him up as magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 下车，先问大姓名主，吏数闾里豪强以对，䊸厉声怒曰：“本问贵戚若马、窦等辈，岂能知此卖菜佣乎？

translations.literal: When he stepped down from his carriage he first asked the great names and their patrons; the clerks answered by listing neighborhood bullies; Xu thundered in rage, “I was asking about honored affines such as the Ma and Dou houses—do you suppose I care about vegetable peddlers?”
translations.idiomatic: On his first day he demanded the names of the truly powerful houses; his clerks offered petty neighborhood thugs; Xu roared, “I meant great in-laws like the Ma and Dou clans—do you think I waste my time on cabbage sellers?”

sentences.zh: ”于是部吏望风旨，争以激切为事。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the section clerks, catching his drift, vied to be harsh and cutting in their work.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates took the hint and competed to outdo one another in severity.

sentences.zh: 贵戚跼蹐，京师肃清。

translations.literal: The imperial in-laws drew in their feet and hands; the capital was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Consort kinsmen walked on tiptoe, and the capital fell quiet.

sentences.zh: 皇后弟黄门郎窦笃从宫中归，夜至止奸亭，亭长霍延遮止笃，笃苍头与争，延遂拔剑拟笃，而肆詈恣口。

translations.literal: The empress’s younger brother, Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Du, was returning from the palace one night and reached the Bastion-against-Lechery post; the post chief Huo Yan barred Du’s passage; Du’s household slave quarreled with Yan, whereupon Yan drew his sword and pointed it at Du while pouring abuse from his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Du, the queen’s brother and a yellow-gate gentleman, was riding home from the palace after dark when post chief Huo Yan stopped him at the “Halt Debauchery” watch; a slave scuffled with the guards, Huo Yan drew steel on Dou Du himself, and reviled him without restraint.

sentences.zh: 笃以表闻。

translations.literal: Du memorialized the affair to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Du reported the incident to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 诏召司隶校尉、河南尹诣尚书谴问，遣剑戟士收䊸送廷尉诏狱。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the Colonel Director of Retainers and the Governor of Henan to the Masters of Writing for a reprimand, and sent halberdiers to seize Xu and deliver him to the imperial prison of the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered both the colonel director of retainers and the governor of Henan hauled before the secretariat for a scolding, then sent armored guards to arrest Zhou Xu and throw him into the commandant’s imperial jail.

sentences.zh: 数日贳出。

translations.literal: Several days later he was released on bail.
translations.idiomatic: After a few days he was bailed out.

sentences.zh: 帝知䊸奉法疾奸，不事贵戚，然苛惨失中，数为有司所奏，八年，遂免官。

translations.literal: The emperor knew that Xu upheld the law and hated villainy and did not truckle to imperial affines, yet his harsh cruelty missed the mean and he was repeatedly memorialized against by the authorities; in the eighth year he was finally removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew Zhou Xu enforced the statutes and despised corruption, and that he bowed to no palace favorite, yet his savagery overshot decency and censors impeached him again and again; in the eighth year of the reign he was dismissed for good.

sentences.zh: 后为御史中丞。

translations.literal: Later he became Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to palace assistant imperial clerk.

sentences.zh: 和帝即位，太傅邓彪奏䊸在任过酷，不宜典司京辇。

translations.literal: When Emperor He ascended the throne, Grand Tutor Deng Biao memorialized that Xu in office had been excessively cruel and was unsuited to oversee the capital precincts.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor He’s accession, Grand Tutor Deng Biao argued that Zhou Xu’s tenure had been too bloody for him to police the capital region.

sentences.zh: 免归田里。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and returned to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank and sent back to his farm.

sentences.zh: 后窦氏贵盛，笃兄弟秉权，睚眦宿怨，无不僵仆。

translations.literal: Later, when the Dou clan grew powerful and Du’s brothers monopolized authority, every old grudge born of a sidelong glance meant someone fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Dou family dominated the government, and Dou Du’s brothers settled every petty score with a corpse.

sentences.zh: 䊸自谓无全，乃柴门自守，以待其祸。

translations.literal: Xu thought he could not preserve his life intact, barred his gate, and guarded himself while awaiting disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xu gave up hope of survival, bolted his gate, and waited for the blow to fall.

sentences.zh: 然笃等以䊸公正，而怨隙有素，遂不敢害。

translations.literal: Yet Du and the others, because Xu was upright and fair and their old resentments ran deep, still dared not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Dou Du and his kin, knowing Zhou Xu’s rectitude and their own long-standing debt to him, never dared touch him.

sentences.zh: 永元五年，复征为御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongyuan he was again summoned as Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan five he was recalled as palace assistant imperial clerk.

sentences.zh: 诸窦虽诛，而夏阳侯□犹尚在朝。

translations.literal: Although the Dou were executed, the Marquis of Xiayang □ was still at court.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou faction had been cut down, but the Marquis of Xiayang □ (the name is lost in the manuscript) still held a post at court.

sentences.zh: 䊸疾之，乃上疏曰：“臣联臧文仲之事君也，见有礼于君者，事之如孝子之养父母，见无礼于君者，诛之如鹰鹯之逐鸟雀。

translations.literal: Xu detested him and presented a memorial: “Your servant has heard how Zang Wenzhong served his lord: those who showed the lord courtesy he served like a filial son nourishing his parents; those who showed the lord no courtesy he executed like a hawk chasing sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xu loathed the man and wrote: “I have read how Zang Wenzhong served his ruler—he honored the respectful as a son cares for his parents, and struck down the disrespectful as a hawk strikes small birds.

sentences.zh: 案夏阳侯□，本出轻薄，志在邪僻，学无经术，而妄构讲舍，外招儒徒，实会奸桀。

translations.literal: Investigate the Marquis of Xiayang □: he sprang from shallow stock, his aims are crooked, he has no classical learning, yet rashly erects lecture halls, outwardly gathers Confucian students, but in truth convenes a pack of villains.
translations.idiomatic: Look at the Marquis of Xiayang □: born of mean families, bent on wickedness, unread in the canon, he throws up lecture halls, recruits scholars as a screen, and secretly collects ruffians.

sentences.zh: 轻忽天威，侮慢王室，又造作巡狩封禅上书，惑众不道，当伏诛戮，而主者营私，不为国计。

translations.literal: He trifles with Heaven’s majesty, insults the royal house, and forges memorials on imperial tours and feng and shan sacrifices to delude the multitude—conduct contrary to the Way—he ought to suffer execution; yet those in charge scheme for private ends and do not act for the state’s good.
translations.idiomatic: He mocks celestial authority, affronts the Liu house, and circulates forged petitions about imperial progresses and feng-shan rites to confuse the people—conduct that deserves death—while officials shield him for private gain instead of serving the realm.”

sentences.zh: 夫涓流虽寡，浸成江河；

translations.literal: Though a trickle is slight, soaking can form a river;
translations.idiomatic: A thin rill, given time, swells into a river;

sentences.zh: 爝火虽微，卒能燎野，履霜有渐，可不惩革？

translations.literal: though a torch-flame is small, it can finally burn the wild; treading frost knows a gradual advance—can we not punish and reform?”
translations.idiomatic: a brand’s flame, however small, can yet scorch the plain; we walk on frost by slow degrees—will you not cut this evil short?”

sentences.zh: 宜寻吕产专窃之乱，永惟王莽篡逆之祸，上安社稷之计，下解万夫之惑。

translations.literal: You should trace the chaos of Lü Chan’s exclusive seizure of power, ever ponder the disaster of Wang Mang’s usurpation, secure the altars of soil and grain above, and below dispel the doubts of the myriad commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Recall the turmoil when Lü Chan monopolized power, remember Wang Mang’s usurpation, steady the altars on high, and quiet the fears of the common people below.”

sentences.zh: ”会瑰归国，䊸迁司隶校尉。

translations.literal: ” At this time Marquis Gui returned to his fief, and Xu was transferred to Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: About then Marquis Gui returned to his estate, and Zhou Xu was shifted to colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，旱，车驾自幸洛阳录囚徒，二人被掠生虫，坐左转骑都尉。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year there was drought; the imperial carriage personally went to Luoyang to review prisoners; two men had been tortured until maggots bred in their wounds; for this he was demoted to Chief Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: That summer’s drought brought the emperor in person to Luoyang to inspect convicts; two prisoners bore worm-eaten wounds from torture, and Zhou Xu was demoted to chief commandant of cavalry for it.

sentences.zh: 七年，迁将作大匠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Court Architect.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became court architect.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 黄昌字圣真，会稽余姚人也。

translations.literal: Huang Chang, courtesy name Shengzhen, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang, courtesy name Shengzhen, hailed from Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 本出孤微。

translations.literal: Originally he came from lonely, humble origins.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been poor and obscure.

sentences.zh: 居近学官，数见诸生修庠序之礼，因好之，遂就经学。

translations.literal: His dwelling lay near the school office; he often saw students performing the rites of the academy and came to love it, whereupon he pursued classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He lived beside the county school, watched the students rehearse academy etiquette, fell in love with scholarship, and took up the classics.

sentences.zh: 又晓习文法，仕郡为决曹。

translations.literal: He also mastered written law and precedent and served the commandery as Clerk of Decisions.
translations.idiomatic: He learned statutes and precedents and became the commandery’s clerk of decisions.

sentences.zh: 刺史行部，见昌，甚奇之，辟从事。

translations.literal: When the Inspector toured his circuit and saw Chang, he greatly marveled at him and summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: An inspecting censor spotted him on tour, was deeply impressed, and took him on as an aide.

sentences.zh: 后拜宛令，政尚严猛，好发奸伏。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Magistrate of Wan; his government favored severity; he liked exposing hidden crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He was later named magistrate of Wan, ruled with a heavy hand, and delighted in digging up concealed wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 人有盗其车盖者，昌初无所言，后乃密遣亲客至门下贼曹家掩取得之，悉收其家，一时杀戮。

translations.literal: When someone stole the canopy of his carriage, Chang at first said nothing; afterward he secretly sent trusted clients to the home of the chief of thieves under the gate office to seize the goods in a raid; he then arrested the whole household and put them all to death at one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: A thief stole his carriage umbrella; Huang Chang said nothing at first, then had confederates raid the chief constable’s house where the loot was hidden, seized the entire family, and executed them all in one sweep.

sentences.zh: 大姓战惧，皆称神明。

translations.literal: The great clans trembled in fear and all called him divine in insight.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful houses shook with fear and hailed him as uncannily perceptive.

sentences.zh: 朝廷举能，迁蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: The court recommended him for ability and promoted him to Prefect of Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for administrative talent, he rose to prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 先太守李根年老多悖政，百姓侵冤。

translations.literal: The previous prefect, Li Gen, was old and much misgoverned, so the common people suffered injustice.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor Li Gen was aged and incompetent, and the people had piled up grievances.

sentences.zh: 及昌到，吏人讼者七百余人，悉为断理，莫不得所。

translations.literal: By the time Chang arrived, more than seven hundred clerks and commoners had suits pending; he settled every case and none failed to obtain what was due.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chang arrived, over seven hundred plaintiffs waited at the yamen; he judged every suit until each party walked away satisfied.

sentences.zh: 密捕盗帅一人，胁使条诸县强暴之人姓名居处，乃分遣掩讨，无有遗脱。

translations.literal: He secretly seized one robber chieftain and coerced him to list by name and dwelling every violent man in the counties; he then sent agents in separate raids to seize them, and none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He captured a bandit chief in secret, forced him to write out every strong-arm man in the commandery with his address, then launched simultaneous roundups so that none slipped away.

sentences.zh: 宿恶大奸，皆奔走他境。

translations.literal: Hardened villains and arch-scoundrels all fled to other jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Career criminals and arch-villains bolted for neighboring provinces.

sentences.zh: 初，昌为州书佐，其妇归宁于家，遇贼被获，遂流转入蜀为人妻。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang was a commandery clerk, his wife had gone home on a visit and was captured by bandits; she was finally traded south into Shu and became another man’s wife.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, while Huang Chang was still a commandery clerk, his wife went home to her parents, was taken by raiders, drifted south into Shu, and married another man.

sentences.zh: 妻子犯事，乃诣昌自讼。

translations.literal: When her son by that household was implicated in an affair, she came to Chang and laid her own complaint.
translations.idiomatic: When a son from that marriage fell afoul of the law, she presented herself before Huang Chang to plead the case herself.

sentences.zh: 昌疑母不为蜀人，因问所由。

translations.literal: Chang doubted that the mother was not a native of Shu and asked how she had come there.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang suspected she was not Shu-born and questioned her background.

sentences.zh: 对曰：“妾本会稽余姚戴次公女，州书佐黄昌妻也。

translations.literal: She answered, “I am originally the daughter of Dai Cigong of Yuyao in Kuaiji, the wife of Huang Chang the commandery clerk.
translations.idiomatic: She said, “I am Dai Cigong’s daughter from Yuyao in Kuaiji—I was once the wife of your clerk Huang Chang.”

sentences.zh: 妾尝归家，为贼所略，遂至于此。

translations.literal: Once when I was visiting home, I was taken by bandits and so came to this place.”
translations.idiomatic: “On a visit home I was carried off by brigands and eventually sold here.”

sentences.zh: ”昌惊，呼前谓曰：“何以识黄昌邪？

translations.literal: ” Chang was stunned, called her forward and said, “How do you know Huang Chang?”
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang started, drew her near, and asked, “How could you know Huang Chang?”

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“昌左足心有黑子，常自言当为二千石。

translations.literal: ” She replied, “Chang has a black mole on the sole of his left foot and used to say he would rise to two-thousand-dan rank.”
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “He has a black mole on the sole of his left foot and used to say he was fated for two-thousand-dan rank.”

sentences.zh: ”昌乃出足示之。

translations.literal: ” Chang then bared his foot and showed her.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled off his boot and showed her the sole.

sentences.zh: 因相持悲泣，还为夫妇。

translations.literal: Thereupon they embraced and wept and became husband and wife again.
translations.idiomatic: They fell weeping into each other’s arms and remarried.

sentences.zh: 视事四年，征，再迁陈相。

translations.literal: After four years in office he was summoned and twice promoted to Chancellor of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Four years into his tenure he was recalled to court and twice promoted to chancellor of Chen.

sentences.zh: 县人彭氏旧豪纵，造起大舍，高楼临道。

translations.literal: In the county the Peng clan had long been arrogant and unrestrained; they built a great residence with a high tower overlooking the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Peng family, old bullies of the county, raised a mansion whose upper gallery overlooked the highway.

sentences.zh: 昌每出行县，彭氏妇人辄升楼而观。

translations.literal: Whenever Chang went on inspection rounds, the women of the Peng family would climb the tower to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huang Chang toured the district, the Peng women climbed that gallery to stare down at him.

sentences.zh: 昌不喜，遂敕收付狱，案杀之。

translations.literal: Chang disliked it, then ordered them seized and jailed, tried them, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The display angered him; he had the women arrested, tried, and put to death.

sentences.zh: 又迁为河内太守，又再迁颍川太守。

translations.literal: He was further transferred to Prefect of Henei, then again promoted to Prefect of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to prefect of Henei, then was raised again to prefect of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 永和五年，征拜将作大匠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghe he was summoned as Court Architect.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe five the court named him court architect.

sentences.zh: 汉安元年，进补大司农，左转太中大夫，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Han’an he was promoted to full Minister of Agriculture, demoted to Grand Palace Counselor, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Han’an one saw him promoted to minister of agriculture, then reduced to grand palace counselor, in which post he died.

sentences.zh: 阳球字方正，渔阳泉州人也。

translations.literal: Yang Qiu, courtesy name Fangzheng, was a native of Quanzhou in Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu, courtesy name Fangzheng, came from Quanzhou in Yuyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世大姓冠盖。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been a great surname of caps and canopies.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long ranked among the great houses whose coaches filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 球能击剑，习弓马。

translations.literal: Qiu could fence with the sword and was practiced in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled with the sword and the bow from horseback.

sentences.zh: 性严厉，好申、韩之学。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and harsh and loved the learning of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.
translations.idiomatic: His temper ran severe, and he favored the legalism of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.

sentences.zh: 郡吏有辱其母者，球结少年数十人，杀吏，灭其家，由是知名。

translations.literal: When a commandery clerk had insulted his mother, Qiu gathered several dozen youths, killed the clerk, and wiped out his family; by this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery clerk had slighted his mother; Yang Qiu rounded up scores of young braves, murdered the man, and exterminated his household—deeds that made his name.

sentences.zh: 初举孝廉，补尚书侍郎，闲达故事，其章奏处议，常为台阁所崇信。

translations.literal: First recommended as filially pious and incorrupt, he was appointed gentleman of the Masters of Writing; thoroughly versed in precedent, his memorials and deliberations were always trusted in the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filially pious and incorrupt, he entered the Masters of Writing as a gentleman, mastered administrative precedent, and won steady confidence for his memorials and opinions.

sentences.zh: 出为高唐令，以严苛过理，郡守收举，会赦见原。

translations.literal: Sent out as Magistrate of Gaotang; for severity beyond reason the prefect ordered his arrest, but a general amnesty spared him.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Gaotang he exceeded all bounds of harshness; the prefect had him arrested, though a general amnesty eventually cleared him.

sentences.zh: 辟司徒刘宠府，举高第。

translations.literal: He was summoned to Minister of Education Liu Chong’s bureau and ranked at the top of his class.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Grand Minister of Education Liu Chong’s staff and placed first in the high-ranking cohort.

sentences.zh: 九江山贼起，连月不解。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Jiujiang and for months could not be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaws erupted in Jiujiang and defied suppression for months on end.

sentences.zh: 三府上球有理奸才，拜九江太守。

translations.literal: The Three Offices memorialized that Qiu had talent for handling villainy, and he was appointed Prefect of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The three highest bureaus reported that Yang Qiu had a gift for crushing crime, and the throne made him prefect of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 球到，设方略，凶贼殄破，收郡中奸吏尽杀之。

translations.literal: When Qiu arrived, he laid plans; the vicious bandits were wiped out, and he seized every villainous clerk in the commandery and had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up a strategy, annihilated the rebel bands, then rounded up every corrupt clerk in the commandery and executed the lot.

sentences.zh: 迁平原相。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chancellor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to chancellor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 出教曰：“相前莅高唐，志埽奸鄙，遂为贵郡所见枉举。

translations.literal: He issued an instruction saying: “Your chancellor formerly governed Gaotang, intent on sweeping away the vile, and was thereupon slandered and impeached by your honorable commandery.”
translations.idiomatic: He published an order: “When last I governed Gaotang I meant to scour out wickedness, and your honorable commandery repaid me with a trumped-up impeachment.”

sentences.zh: 昔桓公释管仲射钩之仇，高祖赦季布逃亡之罪。

translations.literal: “In old times Duke Huan released Duke Guan’s guilt for shooting his hook-buckle, and the Supreme Ancestor pardoned Ji Bu’s crime of flight.”
translations.idiomatic: “Duke Huan of Qi forgave Guan Zhong’s arrow at his belt hook; Gaozu spared Ji Bu the fugitive’s guilt.”

sentences.zh: 虽以不德，敢忘前义。

translations.literal: “Though I lack virtue, how dare I forget such prior righteousness.”
translations.idiomatic: “Though I am a lesser man, I would not forget such magnanimity.”

sentences.zh: 况君臣分定，而可怀宿者哉！

translations.literal: “Moreover, when ruler and minister have fixed roles, who may cling to old resentments!”
translations.idiomatic: “Besides, lord and minister each have a part—who should nurse ancient grudges?”

sentences.zh: 今一蠲往愆，期诸来效。

translations.literal: “Now I once for all wipe away past faults and look to you for future service.”
translations.idiomatic: “Henceforth I cancel old scores and expect new loyalty from you.”

sentences.zh: 若受教之后而不改奸状者，不得复有所容矣。

translations.literal: “If after receiving this instruction you do not reform your villainous conduct, you will find no further tolerance.”
translations.idiomatic: “Anyone who keeps his criminal habits after this warning will find no mercy left.”

sentences.zh: ”郡中咸畏服焉。

translations.literal: ” Throughout the commandery all feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The whole commandery stood in awe and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 时，天下大旱，司空张颢条奏长吏苛酷贪污者，皆罢免之。

translations.literal: At that time a great drought afflicted the realm; Minister of Works Zhang Hao submitted a memorial listing senior officials who were harsh, cruel, or corrupt, and all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: An empire-wide drought struck; Minister of Works Zhang Hao filed charges against magistrates who were brutal or venal, and every one named was removed.

sentences.zh: 球坐严苦，征诣廷尉，当免官。

translations.literal: Qiu, because of his severity, was summoned to the Commandant of Justice and ought to have been dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu’s harshness brought him before the commandant of justice, where the verdict should have stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 灵帝以球九江时有功，拜议郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling, recalling Qiu’s merit at Jiujiang, appointed him gentleman consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling remembered his service in Jiujiang and instead named him gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 迁将作大匠，坐事论。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Court Architect but was sentenced for an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to court architect, then ran afoul of the law and was convicted.

sentences.zh: 顷之，拜尚书令。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Prefect of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became prefect of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 奏罢鸿都文学，曰：

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish the Hongdu literati, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to shut down the Hongdu academy, writing:

sentences.zh: 伏承有诏敕中尚方为鸿都文学乐松、江览等三十二人图象立赞，以劝学者。

translations.literal: “I have heard that an edict ordered the palace workshop to paint portraits with eulogies for thirty-two Hongdu literati such as Yue Song and Jiang Lan, so as to encourage scholars.”
translations.idiomatic: “I learn by edict that the inner workshop is to paint likenesses with encomia for thirty-two Hongdu writers including Yue Song and Jiang Lan, the better to spur learning.”

sentences.zh: 臣闻《传》曰：“君举必书。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the work called Zhuan states, “Whatever the ruler does must be recorded.”
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuan puts it plainly: “The ruler’s every act is entered in the record.”

sentences.zh: 书而不法，后嗣何观！

translations.literal: If it is recorded yet not according to law, what will posterity behold!”
translations.idiomatic: If what is written is lawless, what are later generations to make of it?”

sentences.zh: ”案松、览等皆出于微蔑，斗筲小人，依凭世戚，附托权豪，俯眉承睫，微进明时。

translations.literal: ” Investigating Song, Lan, and the rest, they all sprang from mean obscurity—petty men of bushel-basket capacity—who leaned on consort power, clung to mighty houses, lowered their brows and lifted their lashes, and crept forward in a bright age.
translations.idiomatic: “Song, Lan, and their like rose from utter obscurity—small men who hitched themselves to palace kin and great clans, cringed and flattered, and inched upward in a time that called for clarity.”

sentences.zh: 或献赋一篇，或鸟篆盈简，而位升郎中，形图丹青。

translations.literal: Some presented a single rhapsody, or filled a slip with bird-seal script, yet rose to gentleman of the palace and had their forms painted in vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: Some offered one fu, or a page of ornamental seal script, and won a gentleman’s post and a portrait in the gallery.

sentences.zh: 亦有笔不点牍，辞不辩心，假手请字，妖伪百品，莫不被蒙殊恩，蝉蜕滓浊。

translations.literal: There were also those whose brush never dotted a document, whose words did not express their minds, who had others ghost-write characters—a hundred sorts of sorcery and fraud—yet none failed to receive extraordinary favor and slough off the mire like cicadas.
translations.idiomatic: Others could not compose a line, hired ghostwriters, and traded in every kind of humbug, yet each shed the mud like a cicada and walked away showered with grace.

sentences.zh: 是以有识掩口，天下嗟叹。

translations.literal: Therefore men of insight covered their mouths, and the realm sighed in lament.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful men clapped hands to their lips while the empire groaned.

sentences.zh: 臣闻图象之设，以昭劝戒，欲令人君动鉴得失。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the institution of painted images is meant to display encouragement and warning and to move the ruler’s heart to mirror gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Portraits were meant to teach by example, pricking the sovereign’s conscience with models of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 未闻竖子小人，诈作文颂，而可妄窃天官，垂象图素者也。

translations.literal: I have never heard that striplings and petty men, forging literary praise, may rashly steal celestial offices and hang their likenesses on plain silk.”
translations.idiomatic: I never heard that boys and charlatans, fawning in forged verse, might steal high office and hang their faces on the wall.”

sentences.zh: 今太学、东观足以宣明圣化。

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Academy and the Eastern Lodge suffice to proclaim sagely transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy and the Eastern Lodge already broadcast the sage’s transforming influence.

sentences.zh: 愿罢鸿都之选，以消天下之谤。

translations.literal: I beg to abolish the Hongdu selections so as to dispel slander throughout the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Hongdu appointments be ended and the empire’s gossip silenced.”

sentences.zh: 书奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was presented but drew no response.
translations.idiomatic: The throne filed his paper away without action.

sentences.zh: 时，中常侍王甫、曹节等奸虐弄权，扇动外内，球尝拊髀发愤曰：“若阳球作司隶，此曹子安得容乎？

translations.literal: At that time the Regular Attendants Wang Fu and Cao Jie practiced villainy and toyed with power, fanning intrigue inside and out; Qiu once smote his thigh in fury and said, “If Yang Qiu were colonel director of retainers, how could such vermin be tolerated?”
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch attendants Wang Fu and Cao Jie ran wild; Yang Qiu once struck his thigh and swore, “Give me the colonel’s baton and this rabble would not last a day!”

sentences.zh: ”光和二年，迁为司隶校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guanghe he was transferred to Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghe two he became colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 王甫休沐里舍，球诣阙谢恩，奏收甫及中常侍淳于登、袁赦、封{曰羽}、中黄门刘毅、小黄门庞训、硃禹、齐盛等，及子弟为守令者，奸猾纵恣，罪合灭族。

translations.literal: Wang Fu was resting at his suburban residence; Qiu went to the palace to give thanks for favor and memorialized to arrest Fu, together with Regular Attendants Chunyu Deng, Yuan She, Feng (his personal name is corrupt in the received text), Palace Attendant Liu Yi, Junior Attendants Pang Training, Zhu Yu, Qi Sheng, and others, and those of their sons and younger kin who held prefectures or magistracies—crafty, wanton, crimes deserving extermination of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu was on leave at his villa; Yang Qiu thanked the emperor at court, then filed charges to seize Wang Fu, the attendants Chunyu Deng, Yuan She, Feng (his given name is damaged in the manuscripts), Liu Yi, Pang Training, Zhu Yu, Qi Sheng, and every kinsman serving as a local magistrate—men whose crimes called for wiping out whole clans.

sentences.zh: 太尉段颎谄附佞幸，宜并诛戮。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Duan Jiong fawned on the favorites and ought likewise to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Duan Jiong had curried favor with the clique and should die with them.

sentences.zh: 于是悉收甫、颎等送洛阳狱，及甫子永乐少府萌、沛相吉。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were arrested—Fu, Jiong, and the rest—and sent to the Luoyang prison, together with Fu’s son Meng, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues of Yongle, and Ji, Chancellor of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Wang Fu, Duan Jiong, and their confederates for the Luoyang jail, including Wang Fu’s son Wang Meng, chamberlain for the palace revenues at Yongle, and the chancellor of Pei, Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 球自临考甫等，五毒备极。

translations.literal: Qiu personally presided over the interrogation of Fu and the others, employing every extremity of the five tortures.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu himself examined Wang Fu’s party and applied the full fivefold torments.

sentences.zh: 萌谓球曰：“父子既当伏诛，少以楚毒假借老父。

translations.literal: Meng said to Qiu, “Father and son deserve execution; grant a little respite from Chu torture for my aged father.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng begged, “We are doomed—only spare my old father the worst of the Chu rack.”

translations.literal: The line is a closing quotation mark punctuating Wang Meng’s preceding speech.
translations.idiomatic: The plea from Wang Meng ends here with a closing quotation mark.

sentences.zh: 球曰：“若罪恶无状，死不灭责，乃欲求假借邪？

translations.literal: Qiu said, “If your crimes are beyond description, death does not cancel the debt—do you still ask for leniency?”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu replied, “Your guilt is unspeakable; not even death pays the score—do you still beg indulgence?”

sentences.zh: ”萌乃骂曰：“尔前奉事吾父子如奴，如敢反汝主乎！

translations.literal: ” Meng then cursed, saying, “In times past you waited on us father and son like a slave—dare you now turn against your masters!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng snarled, “You used to serve my father and me like a house slave—how dare you bite the hand that fed you!”

sentences.zh: 今日困吾，行自及也！

translations.literal: “Today you have me cornered, but the blow will soon rebound on you!”
translations.idiomatic: “You have me trapped today, but your own turn comes next!”

sentences.zh: ”球使以土窒萌口，箠朴交至，父子悉死杖下。

translations.literal: ” Qiu had earth stuffed into Meng’s mouth; clubs and cudgels rained down until father and son both died beneath the rods.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu ordered Meng’s mouth packed with mud; the beaters fell on them until father and son perished under the clubs.

sentences.zh: 颎亦自杀。

translations.literal: Jiong also committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong killed himself.

sentences.zh: 乃僵磔甫尸于夏城门，大署榜曰“贼臣王甫”。

translations.literal: He then had Fu’s corpse stretched on the rack and dismembered at the Summer Gate, posting a large placard that read “The traitorous minister Wang Fu.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu’s corpse was dismembered and displayed at the Summer Gate under a placard: “The traitor minister Wang Fu.”

sentences.zh: 尽没入财产，妻、子皆徙比景。

translations.literal: All property was confiscated; wives and children were banished to Bijin.
translations.idiomatic: Their goods went to the treasury and their families were exiled to Bijin on the southern sea.

sentences.zh: 球既诛甫，复欲以次表曹节等，乃敕中都官从事曰：“且先去大猾，当次案豪右。

translations.literal: After Qiu had executed Fu, he wished next to memorialize against Cao Jie and the rest; he therefore instructed the chief clerk of the capital district: “First remove the great villains; next we shall investigate the mighty houses.”
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Fu gone, Yang Qiu meant to impeach Cao Jie next; he told his chief clerk, “Cut down the chief monsters first; then we take the great clans.”

sentences.zh: ”权门闻之，莫不屏气。

translations.literal: When the powerful families heard this, none dared draw breath.
translations.idiomatic: The great houses heard and held their breath.

sentences.zh: 诸奢饰之物，皆各缄滕，不敢陈设。

translations.literal: Every article of luxury was wrapped and sealed away; none dared display it.
translations.idiomatic: Ornaments of every kind were boxed and hidden; no one flaunted wealth.

sentences.zh: 京师畏震。

translations.literal: The capital trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang shook with dread.

sentences.zh: 时，顺帝虞贵人葬，百官会丧还，曹节见磔甫尸道次，慨然抆泪曰：“我曹自可相食，何宜使犬舐其汁乎？

translations.literal: At that time, when Honored Lady Yu of Emperor Shun was buried, the hundred officials returned from the funeral; Cao Jie saw Fu’s dismembered corpse by the road, wiped tears in indignation, and said, “We may devour one another among ourselves—how can we let dogs lick our juices?”
translations.idiomatic: At Lady Yu’s funeral the courtiers passed Wang Fu’s remains; Cao Jie wept with rage and said, “We eunuchs may tear each other apart, but we must not become carrion for curs.”

sentences.zh: ”语诸常侍，今且俱入，勿过里舍也。

translations.literal: ” He told the other regular attendants, “For now let us all enter together; do not stop by our suburban houses.”
translations.idiomatic: He warned his fellow attendants, “We go straight into the palace together—no one detours home to his villa.”

sentences.zh: 节直入省，白帝曰：“阳球故酷暴吏，前三府奏当免官，以九江微功，复见擢用。

translations.literal: Jie went straight into the palace precincts and reported to the emperor: “Yang Qiu was formerly a cruel clerk; the Three Offices memorialized that he should be dismissed, yet for slight merit at Jiujiang he was promoted again.”
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie burst in on the emperor: “Yang Qiu was a savage underling; the three bureaus voted to cashier him, then a tiny deed at Jiujiang bought him back.”

sentences.zh: 愆过之人，好为妄作，不宜使在司隶，以骋毒虐。

translations.literal: A man prone to fault loves reckless action; he must not be left as colonel director of retainers to vent poisonous cruelty.”
translations.idiomatic: A man who piles up offenses delights in mischief; he cannot hold the colonel’s rod without turning it into torture.”

sentences.zh: ”帝乃徙球为卫尉。

translations.literal: ” The emperor thereupon transferred Qiu to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moved Yang Qiu to commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 时，球出谒陵，节敕尚书令召拜，不得稽留尺一。

translations.literal: At that time Qiu had gone out to attend the imperial tombs; Jie ordered the Prefect of the Masters of Writing to summon him with an appointment edict and allow not the slightest delay.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Qiu was away at the mausoleums, Cao Jie forced the prefect of the Masters of Writing to issue his transfer instantly, brooking no delay.

sentences.zh: 球被召急，因求见帝，叩头曰：“臣无清高之行，横蒙鹰犬之任。

translations.literal: Qiu, urgently summoned, begged an audience with the emperor and kowtowed, saying, “Your servant lacks the conduct of lofty purity yet has rashly received the commission of a hawk hound.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu raced back, forced his way to audience, and kowtowed: “I am no saint, yet you made me your bird of prey.”

sentences.zh: 前虽纠诛王甫、段颎、盖简落狐狸，未足宣示天下。

translations.literal: Though I earlier impeached and executed Wang Fu and Duan Jiong, that was merely like clearing away a few foxes—not enough to proclaim justice to the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: “Killing Wang Fu and Duan Jiong only swept aside a handful of foxes; the realm has not yet seen the full reckoning I promised.”

sentences.zh: 愿假臣一月，必令豺狼鸱枭，各服其辜。

translations.literal: Grant your servant one month more, and I shall make wolves and owls each suffer their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: “Give me one more month and I will bring every jackal and kite to book.”

sentences.zh: ”叩头流血。

translations.literal: ” He kowtowed until the blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: He beat his head on the floor until blood ran.

sentences.zh: 殿上呵叱曰：“卫尉扞诏邪！

translations.literal: Those on the dais shouted, “Does the Commandant of the Guards defy an edict!”
translations.idiomatic: Voices from the steps roared, “Does the commandant of the guards reject the imperial command?”

sentences.zh: ”至于再三，乃受拜。

translations.literal: ” This was repeated three times before he accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Three times they thundered the order before he took the seal.

sentences.zh: 其冬，司徒刘郃与球议收案张让、曹节，节等知之，共诬白郃等。

translations.literal: That winter Minister of Education Liu He plotted with Qiu to arrest Zhang Rang and Cao Jie; when Jie learned of it, they jointly slandered Liu He and the others.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Minister of Education Liu He and Yang Qiu planned to seize Zhang Rang and Cao Jie; the eunuchs struck first with forged accusations.

sentences.zh: 语已见《陈球传》。

translations.literal: The account is already given in the “Biography of Chen Qiu.”
translations.idiomatic: The story is told in full in the biography of Chen Qiu.

sentences.zh: 遂收球送洛阳狱，诛死，妻、子徙边。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qiu was seized and sent to the Luoyang prison, put to death, and his wife and children banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu was thrown into the Luoyang jail, executed, and his family driven to the border.

sentences.zh: 王吉者，陈留浚仪人，中常侍甫之养子也。

translations.literal: Wang Ji was a man of Junyi in Chenliu, the adopted son of Regular Attendant Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji of Junyi in Chenliu was the adopted son of the attendant Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 甫在《宦者传》。

translations.literal: Fu appears in the “Biographies of the Palace Attendants.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu’s life is recorded among the palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 吉少好诵读书传，喜名声，而性残忍。

translations.literal: In youth Ji loved to recite texts and histories and delighted in reputation, yet his nature was cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji loved books and fame from boyhood, but his heart was pitiless.

sentences.zh: 以父秉权宠，年二十余，为沛相。

translations.literal: Because his father wielded favor and power, at little more than twenty sui he became Chancellor of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: His father’s influence won him, before thirty, the chancellorship of Pei.

sentences.zh: 晓达政事，能断察疑狱，发起奸伏，多出众议。

translations.literal: He was conversant with administration, able to decide doubtful suits, expose hidden crimes, and often surpassed others’ counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the machinery of government, settled hard cases, dug out concealed guilt, and routinely outshone other men’s advice.
