sentences.zh: 课使郡内各举奸吏豪人诸常有微过酒肉为臧者，虽数十年犹如贬弃，注其名籍。

translations.literal: He ordered each district within the commandery to denounce crafty clerks and powerful men—any who had ever taken wine or meat as bribes, even decades before—and struck them from the rolls as if newly disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: He made every county report venal clerks and magnates, even those who long ago had taken a jug of wine as a bribe, and struck their names from office as though the crime were fresh.

sentences.zh: 专选剽悍吏，击断非法。

translations.literal: He chose only fierce clerks and struck down offenders outside the law.
translations.idiomatic: He picked the most brutal bailiffs and had them kill beyond the statutes.

sentences.zh: 若有生子不养，即斩其父母，合土棘埋之。

translations.literal: If someone bore a child and did not rear it, he beheaded the parents and buried them packed with thorns.
translations.idiomatic: Parents who refused to raise a newborn were beheaded and heaped in a pit with thorns.

sentences.zh: 凡杀人皆磔尸车上，随其罪目。

translations.literal: Every homicide ended with the corpse dismembered on a cart according to the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Each murderer’s body was torn apart on a cart, labeled with his crimes.

sentences.zh: 宣示属县。

translations.literal: This was displayed through the subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: The carts toured every county as a warning.

sentences.zh: 夏月腐烂，则以绳连其骨，周遍一郡乃止，见者骇惧。

translations.literal: In summer, when putrefaction set in, he strung the bones on ropes and circled the whole commandery before stopping; those who saw it were horrified.
translations.idiomatic: When summer heat rotted the flesh, he threaded the skeletons on cords and dragged them through the commandery until onlookers fainted with fear.

sentences.zh: 视事五年，凡杀万余人。

translations.literal: In five years of holding office he killed more than ten thousand people in all.
translations.idiomatic: Five years in office cost over ten thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 其余惨毒刺刻，不可胜数。

translations.literal: The rest of his savagery and poison cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The other atrocities beggar enumeration.

sentences.zh: 郡中惴恐，莫敢自保。

translations.literal: The commandery quaked in terror; none dared trust to his own safety.
translations.idiomatic: The whole region lived in dread, sure that no one was safe.

sentences.zh: 及阳球奏甫，乃就收执，死于洛阳狱。

translations.literal: When Yang Qiu impeached Wang Fu, Ji was at last arrested and died in the Luoyang prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu’s indictment of Wang Fu finally landed Wang Ji in the Luoyang jail, where he died.

sentences.zh: 论曰：古者郭□，善恶易分。

translations.literal: The essayist remarks: In antiquity the wards of Guo □ made good and evil easy to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In high antiquity the ward system—here the text reads Guo □—kept virtue and vice plain to see.

sentences.zh: 至于画衣冠，异服色，而莫之犯。

translations.literal: When it came to painting caps and robes and varying garment colors, none violated the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages marked criminals by dress and insignia, and the law scarcely needed blood.

sentences.zh: 叔世偷薄，上下相蒙，德义不足以相洽，化导不能以惩违，遂乃严刑痛杀，随而绳之，致刻深之吏，以暴理奸，倚疾邪之公直，济忍苛之虐情。

translations.literal: In a decadent age men grew thin in honesty; high and low deceived one another; virtue and righteousness no longer knit society together, instruction could not punish transgressions, and so harsh punishments and painful executions followed, the rope of law dragged after—whereupon deeply carving clerks used violence to manage villainy, leaned on a twisted notion of blunt integrity, and indulged their appetite for pitiless cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When the age turned mean, ruler and ruled lied to each other, moral suasion failed, and only the rack remained; “capable” cruel officials mistook brutality for justice and called their spite zeal.

sentences.zh: 汉世所谓酷能者，盖有闻也。

translations.literal: The so-called “capable cruel officials” of Han times were roughly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the Han’s famous “ruthless talents.”

sentences.zh: 皆以敢捍精敏，巧附文理，风行霜烈，威誉喧赫。

translations.literal: All were bold, keen, clever at attaching phrases to statutes, swift as wind and bitter as frost, their dread reputations thundering abroad.
translations.idiomatic: They were fearless, sharp, masters of legal wording, swift as a gale, loud as thunder.

sentences.zh: 与夫断断守道之吏，何工否之殊乎！

translations.literal: How wide is the gulf between them and the clerk who stubbornly keeps the Way!
translations.idiomatic: What a distance lies between such men and the official who simply holds fast to the right!

sentences.zh: 故严君蚩黄霸之术，密人笑卓茂之政，猛既穷矣，而犹或未胜。

translations.literal: Hence Lord Yan mocked Huang Ba’s methods, and the people of Mi laughed at Zhuo Mao’s government—severity pushed to the limit still could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: So Yan Gongyan sneered at Huang Ba’s soft ways, and Mi county mocked Zhuo Mao’s kindness—yet even the harshest rule could not win the day.

sentences.zh: 然硃邑不以笞辱加物，袁安未尝鞫人臧罪，而猾恶自禁，人不敢犯。

translations.literal: Yet Zhu Yi never added the shame of flogging to others, and Yuan An never tortured men for embezzlement, yet the crafty and wicked restrained themselves of their own accord, and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi never flogged a man for show, Yuan An never extorted confessions of graft, yet villains held their tongues and the people kept the peace.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why was that?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 以为威辟既用，而苟免这行兴；

translations.literal: Because once awe by punishment is deployed, conduct that barely escapes wrongdoing flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: When terror is the tool, men scramble only to slip through the cracks;

sentences.zh: 仁信道孚，故感被之情著。

translations.literal: when benevolence and good faith win trust, the feeling of grateful acceptance shines forth.
translations.idiomatic: when kindness and truth are trusted, gratitude takes root.

sentences.zh: 苟免者威隙则奸起，感被者人亡而思存。

translations.literal: Those who barely escape breed intrigue whenever the terror lifts; those who feel acceptance remember their ruler long after he is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Men who obey only the lash plot the moment the lash lifts; men who are moved by grace remember their lord when he is dust.

sentences.zh: 由一邦以言天下，则刑讼繁措，可得而求乎！

translations.literal: Extrapolate from one commandery to the whole realm—then the burden of lawsuits and punishments may be reckoned!”
translations.idiomatic: Judge the whole empire by one county, and you can tally the cost in trials and torments.”

sentences.zh: 赞曰：大道既往，刑礼为薄。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When the great Way has passed away, punishments and rites grow thin.
translations.idiomatic: The hymn runs: The great Way gone, law and ritual wear thin.

sentences.zh: 斯人斯矣，机诈萌作。

translations.literal: Such men appear, and scheming fraud arises.
translations.idiomatic: Such men arise, and deceit sprouts with them.

sentences.zh: 去杀由仁，济宽非虐。

translations.literal: Doing away with killing proceeds from benevolence; aiding leniency is not cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Sparing life begins in humaneness; tempering severity is not softness.

sentences.zh: 末暴虽胜，崇本或略。

translations.literal: Though the violence of the age may win for a moment, the root of reverence may still be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Brutal methods may score a quick gain, yet the deeper root of respect is easily forgotten.
